species.name: Concrete real-world precedent as evidence
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment cites a specific real, named case, company, incident, or historical precedent (not a hypothetical) as direct evidence for its claim, with enough detail to identify it. Score 0 if all evidence is abstract, generic, or purely hypothetical with no named real instance.
species.rationale: R55 grounds its objection in the named bankruptcy of Sam Kane Beef Processors LLC as proof a trust doesn't protect sellers; R45 contrasts the proposed control plan against the actual, named Argentine ant eradication program on Santa Cruz Island. Both R55 and R45 are dense_high_card_low, suggesting the dense model rewards this evidentiary move that a checklist scorecard may not specifically probe for.

species.name: Explicit engagement with counter-arguments
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies at least one specific objection, trade-off, or opposing consideration to its own position and directly responds to it with reasoning. Score 0 if the comment argues in only one direction and never acknowledges any opposing consideration.
species.rationale: R11 explicitly takes on the roe-quality argument for combining pollock seasons and rebuts it with 2019-vs-2020 water-temperature and maturity data; R52 raises and addresses its own worry about needing an AWOS/ASOS alongside its support for the airspace proposal. Both are dense_high_card_low.

species.name: First-hand operational experience with regulated activity
species.instruction: Score 10 if the commenter describes their own direct, specific experience actually performing or being subject to the regulated activity (e.g., a fisher describing a season they fished, a driver describing using a feature), with concrete operational detail. Score 0 if the comment shows no first-hand experience with the activity, only general or secondhand knowledge.
species.rationale: R21 describes the fisher's own participation in the January 2020 voluntary stand-down and its specific dates; R05 describes the commenter's actual day-to-day use of a rearview camera's brightness/contrast controls. Contrast with R08's generic coalition advocacy letter, which contains no first-hand operational account despite being well-organized (dense_low_card_high).
all_names: First-hand operational experience with regulated activity

species.name: Numbers tied to the rule's specific mechanics
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment supplies numeric figures (percentages, dollar amounts, durations, thresholds) that are explicitly tied to how the specific provision under review operates. Score 0 if the comment contains no such rule-specific numbers, or only generic/unrelated statistics.
species.rationale: R31 gives the exact percentages of intersection-event time captured at 15/18.6/20 seconds to justify the EDR recording duration; R11 gives per-zone AFA sideboard limit percentages (Shumagin 0.6047, Chirikof 0.1167, Kodiak 0.2028). Both dense_high_card_low.
all_names: Numbers tied to the rule's specific mechanics

species.name: Identifies unresolved edge case in rule text
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment describes a specific concrete scenario that the proposed rule's text does not clearly address, and explains why the ambiguity matters in practice. Score 0 if the comment raises no such gap or scenario.
species.rationale: R01 flags the increasing concentration of outlier payments as something CMS has not analyzed and asks for a specific reconciliation policy; R60 raises the concrete cross-service gap of how Air Force, Army, Navy, and Marine Corps providers with different existing processes will be trained and transitioned. Both dense_high_card_low.
all_names: Identifies unresolved edge case in rule text

species.name: Verifiable citation to external primary source
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment cites a specific external study, report, or dataset with enough identifying detail (author/agency, year, and page/section/table) that a reader could locate and check it. Score 0 if the comment cites no external sources, or only vague unattributed appeals like 'studies show'.
species.rationale: R45 cites Menke & Holway (2006) and Menke, Fisher, Jetz & Holway (2007) Ecology 88:3164-3175 by name; R24 cites the specific SIGAR report (SIGAR-20-25-SP) with its URL and exact contractor casualty counts (127 vs. 2,214). Both dense_high_card_low, indicating the dense model may reward verifiable sourcing that a checklist scorecard treats no differently from unsupported assertion.
all_names: Verifiable citation to external primary source

species.name: Explicit causal-mechanism / behavioral-response reasoning
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment lays out a specific step-by-step causal chain (including, where relevant, how affected parties will change their behavior) connecting the rule to its claimed consequence, rather than merely asserting the consequence. Score 0 if the comment asserts a harm or benefit with no explanation of the mechanism producing it.
species.rationale: R55 traces trust requirement -> less money available to dealers -> increased lender risk -> higher borrowing cost -> reduced buying capacity -> lower prices for sellers; R11 explains how a combined season increases lucrative incentive for AFA non-exempt vessels to enter the GOA fishery and why that harms Gulf-dependent boats. Both dense_high_card_low.
all_names: Causal mechanism from rule to consequence

species.name: Self-aware concession about own position's limits
species.instruction: Score 10 if the commenter explicitly concedes a real limitation, cost, or complication of the position they are advocating for. Score 0 if the comment is purely one-sided advocacy with no self-critical acknowledgment.
species.rationale: R01 states 'we agree with the intent to modify the measure... we would instead propose to consider removal' rather than simply rejecting CMS's goal; R52 supports the Class E proposal but flags its own concern that the airport still lacks AWOS/ASOS. Both dense_high_card_low.
all_names: Self-aware concession about own position's limits

species.name: Actionable amendment precision
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies precise replacement language, thresholds, definitions, procedures, or parameters; score 0 when the requested action is only “do more,” “act quickly,” or approval/rejection.
species.rationale: R26 proposes text and justification, R41 requests clarification of a specific phrase, and R47 identifies a precise compliance-period change; R10 and R53 remain broadly directive.
all_names: Precision of the specific action requested

species.name: Identifies a conflated distinction the rule misses
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies two or more meaningfully different sub-cases, categories, or entities that the proposed rule treats identically, and explains the resulting problem. Score 0 if the comment does not draw any such distinction.
species.rationale: R07 argues vegetable seed (sold by count) is wrongly folded into rules built for crop seed (sold by weight); R60 argues Air Force's centralized simple-form process, Army's electronic MTF-routed process, and Navy/Marine Corps needs are meaningfully different and shouldn't be handled as one transition. Both dense_high_card_low.
all_names: Identifies a conflated distinction the rule misses

species.name: Geographic or institutional specificity of third-party impact
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment ties its claimed impact to a specific, named place, community, facility, or institution, with enough detail that the impact could be checked or located. Score 0 if the claimed impact is described only in generic, unlocalized terms (e.g., 'the public', 'the economy').
species.rationale: R50 and R57 both describe specific health effects (asthma, cancers) among named neighbors living downwind of auto and steel plants in northeast Ohio tied to the specific SIP provision at issue. Both dense_high_card_low.
all_names: Geographic or institutional specificity of third-party impact

species.name: Feasible alternative design
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment offers an implementable alternative, exception, threshold, or safeguard and explains how it preserves the proposal’s legitimate objective; score 0 when it offers only approval, rejection, or an unelaborated demand.
species.rationale: R07 proposes specific testing and documentation distinctions, and R59 suggests status tracking and an additional criterion; both contrast with comments offering only broad positions such as R25.
all_names: Offers an alternative specific enough for the agency to draft

species.name: Direct correction of the agency's own proposal text
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment quotes or closely paraphrases specific language from the proposed rule itself and identifies a specific error, ambiguity, or misstatement in it, explaining the correct reading. Score 0 if the comment does not engage with the specific wording of the proposal at all.
species.rationale: R18 quotes the proposed 'uninterrupted power supply' language and asks 'Did you mean Transfer to an Emergency power supply?', explaining the UPS-vs-generator distinction; R54 quotes the proposed Section 401 language and argues it contradicts the Supreme Court's PUD No. 1 v. Washington Dept of Ecology holding, noting the agency relies on the dissent. Both dense_low_card_high, so this criterion tests whether the scorecard's high scores here are picking up genuine textual engagement the dense model underweights.
all_names: Direct correction of the agency's own proposal text

species.name: Concretely described personal stake in the outcome
species.instruction: Score 10 if the commenter describes a specific, concrete way that they personally (or their household/business) have been or will be affected by the rule or underlying problem, beyond stating an opinion. Score 0 if the comment expresses only a general opinion with no described personal consequence.
species.rationale: R10 describes the commenter's house being completely destroyed by the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire and the specific difficulty she had finding submission links despite being an experienced consultant; R50 describes living downwind of auto/steel plants and neighbors developing asthma and cancer. Both dense_high_card_low.
all_names: Concretely described personal stake in the outcome

species.name: Identifies conflict with another statute, rule, order, or decision
species.instruction: Score whether the comment locates the proposal against the surrounding legal or regulatory landscape and identifies a specific inconsistency. 10 = a particular other instrument is named (statute section, other rule or AD, court decision, executive order, constitutional provision) and the concrete inconsistency with the proposal is explained. 5 = a general appeal to law, precedent, or 'other agency rules' with nothing named. 0 = the proposal is evaluated in isolation.
species.rationale: R50 (dense 0.452, card 0.997) is four sentences and finds a real collision: this NPRM demands the MA30A1017 actuator within 24 months while AD 2016-04-20 and NPRM 2015-NM-094-AD allow 60 months for the same part. R21 and R26 (dense 0.657 / 0.676, card 0.107 / 0.110) both invoke section 110(k)(6) error correction and the claim that EPA acted unlawfully in removing the Air Nuisance Rule without assessing county-level effects — a procedural-legality argument buried inside otherwise campaign-shaped text, which is very likely part of why dense rates those two far above the card. R37 identifies that the proposal contradicts PUD No. 1 v. Washington Dept. of Ecology and leans on that decision's dissent. R39 names the Appointments Clause, the APA, Knight Hawk, and Prairie State.
all_names: Reconciles the rule against other specific rules or dockets
Identifies conflict with another statute, rule, order, or decision

species.name: Concrete disconfirming instance against the proposal's factual premise
species.instruction: Score how far the comment supplies a specific, checkable real-world instance that cuts against a premise the proposed action depends on. 10 = the comment names a particular event, case, program, dataset, or observation (identifiable by name, date, docket, or document) AND states explicitly why that instance contradicts or materially limits the agency's stated premise. 5 = a specific instance is supplied but its bearing on the agency's premise is left for the reader to infer, or the instance is only loosely tied to the premise. 0 = disagreement is carried entirely by opinion, prediction, preference, or generic assertion, with no instance the agency could go look at.
species.rationale: R03 defeats the premise of a livestock dealer trust by naming the Sam Kane Beef Processors bankruptcy, where a Packers Trust existed and sellers were still left unpaid; that single named instance does more work than the rest of a very short letter, and it sits at dense_pct=0.652 with card_pct=0.154. R54 does the same to the roe-maturity rationale for combining seasons, using the March 2020 acoustic-trawl survey (2.7 C vs a 3.7 C 40-year average; 92.33% vs 74.72% pre-spawning) — dense 0.854, card 0.176. R35 similarly limits the report's Argentine-ant claim by naming what the published soil-moisture studies do and do not establish. On the other side, R38 and R30 assert impacts with no instance at all and are card-high (0.989, 0.891). A bank that credits 'provides evidence' generically cannot distinguish a decisive counterexample from a decorative fact.
all_names: Concrete disconfirming instance against the proposal's factual premise

species.name: Engages the rule's own preamble, analysis, or cited studies
species.instruction: Score whether the comment reasons about the agency's own stated basis for the action rather than about the topic in the abstract. 10 = the comment quotes, cites, or accurately restates the agency's reasoning, its regulatory-impact or cost figures, the statutory mandate it is implementing, or the specific studies the preamble relies on, and then argues from that material. 5 = the agency's rationale is gestured at ('the proposal says it will improve safety') without any of its specifics being handled. 0 = the comment never touches the agency's stated reasoning; it argues for or against the policy on general grounds only.
species.rationale: R11 (dense 0.895, card 0.380) reconstructs the FAST Act mandate and NHTSA's own duration study before commenting — 5 s at 2 Hz to 20 s at 10 Hz, and the 15 s / 18.6 s / 20 s capture results. R47 (dense 0.902, card 0.311) takes EPA's own cost analysis and nets the roughly $15 million per year of added leakage against the claimed savings of just over $24 million. R18 (dense 0.685, card 0.184) attacks the quality of the epidemiology data used to calibrate and validate EPA's perchlorate model. All three are dense-high/card-low. Card-high rows R30, R36, R31 never touch agency reasoning at all. This is the single most consistent property of the dense_high_card_low half and looks like the clearest thing the bank is missing.
all_names: Engages the rule's own preamble, analysis, or cited studies

species.name: Names a specific omission or missing commitment in the proposal
species.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies something the proposal fails to say, define, decide, or commit to, at a level of specificity the agency could act on. 10 = the comment points to a particular gap — an unaddressed scenario, an undelivered commitment, an unassigned responsibility, an unanswered question the rule creates — and says what filling it would require. 5 = the comment says the proposal is incomplete or 'falls short' without locating the gap. 0 = the comment engages only what the proposal does say, or offers no gap analysis at all.
species.rationale: R58 (dense 0.687, card 0.179) is otherwise campaign-shaped but pins a real omission: the draft lead strategy does not commit to lower acceptable levels for lead-based paint and does not commit to speedy replacement of lead service lines. R25 (dense 0.636, card 0.102) is five sentences long and consists almost entirely of an unassigned-responsibility gap: who trains USAF providers to screen a USMC dependent, and where do the forms go. R32 finds the same kind of hole from the other side (how contingent restitution orders are to be categorized under 6050X). R35 finds it in the science report's pollination biology. Comments that are short and template-flavored can still score very high here, which is exactly where scorecard and dense diverge.
all_names: Names a specific omission or missing commitment in the proposal

species.name: Operator-level implementation path: who does what, with what systems
species.instruction: Score how concretely the comment traces what compliance would actually require of the people and systems that must execute it. 10 = the comment describes the existing workflow, equipment, or organizational process in operational detail and shows precisely where the proposal breaks, strains, or is silent about it. 5 = the comment says compliance would be burdensome or infeasible but describes the workflow only in general terms. 0 = no engagement with execution; the comment stays at the level of whether the policy is good or bad.
species.rationale: R25 (dense 0.636, card 0.102) contrasts the Air Force's centralized office and simple form against the Army's electronic routing through military treatment facilities, and asks how the Navy and Marine Corps transition. R12 (dense 0.212, card 0.787) is dense-low but shows the shape of the property well: UPS versus generator transfer, bi-annual preventive maintenance and monthly testing, on-the-fly BAS value changes versus offline uploads. R56 (dense 0.826, card 0.292) supplies the same texture from a delivery driver's seat — monitor brightness and contrast controls, interlock interactions, non-backing uses. The dense-high cases pair the operational detail with a decision the agency must make; the card-high ones often supply detail without that hook.
all_names: Operator-level implementation path: who does what, with what systems

species.name: Burden incidence stated together with the mechanism producing it
species.instruction: Score whether the comment says who specifically gains or bears cost AND by what mechanism, so the incidence claim is inspectable. 10 = named classes of affected party are matched to a stated transmission path (this requirement raises this cost for this actor, which changes this behavior, which lands on this other party). 5 = affected parties are named and costs asserted, but no mechanism links them. 0 = costs or benefits are invoked in the aggregate ('this will hurt the economy') with neither party nor mechanism specified.
species.rationale: R13 (dense 0.857, card 0.309) is a plainly written lay comment that nonetheless gets the incidence right: manufacturers who already meet the requirement face no changeover cost, machine operators avoid the separate calorie-declaration cost, and consumers gain the information — three parties, three mechanisms. R16 (dense 0.548, card 0.045) traces a millions-of-dollars PMTA path to the exit of sub-$5-million firms and to market concentration in the incumbents the rule is aimed at. R03 chains a dealer trust to reduced working capital, higher lender risk, contracted financing, reduced buying capacity, and finally to prices received by all livestock sellers. All three are card-low. Card-high R22 and R38 assert economic impact with no mechanism.
all_names: Burden incidence stated together with the mechanism producing it

species.name: Flags an ambiguous term and shows the interpretive consequence
species.instruction: Score whether the comment isolates a specific word, phrase, or definition in the regulatory text and demonstrates that it admits more than one reading with different practical results. 10 = the term is quoted or cited to its section, at least two readings are laid out, and the divergent consequence of each is stated. 5 = the comment says a term is unclear or asks for a definition without showing what turns on it. 0 = no engagement with the operative text's wording.
species.rationale: R01 (dense 0.916, card 0.333) quotes the proposed 201.2(q) definition of coated seed and separately shows that a rule framework built on weight collides with vegetable seed sold by count — a definitional mismatch running through the whole submission. R32 (dense 0.150, card 0.673) lays out both readings of 'ordered to be paid' (the amount at settlement versus the amount actually disbursed years later) and shows they produce different reported figures. R12 and R15 do the same for 'uninterruptible versus emergency power supply', 'not working properly', and 'conventional manufacturer'. This is textual craft that a bank keyed to argument quality or evidence will read as mere nitpicking, yet it is exactly the kind of comment that changes final rule language.
all_names: Flags an ambiguous term and shows the interpretive consequence

species.name: Position developed through a described, testable deliberative process
species.instruction: Score whether the comment describes how its position was arrived at across the affected parties it speaks for, in a way a reader could interrogate. 10 = the comment states the process — deliberation among affected parties, reconciliation of divergent sub-interests, explicit coordination with or incorporation of other filings — and shows the position survived that process, including where sub-groups differ. 5 = the comment asserts it speaks for many affected parties but describes no process by which their views were gathered or reconciled. 0 = no indication that the position reflects anything beyond a single unexamined view.
species.rationale: R01 (dense 0.916, card 0.333) opens by describing multiple meetings across a broad representation of affected parties to reach consensus, then explicitly flags where sub-sectors diverge (vegetable and conservation seed have different economics from crop seed) rather than papering over it. R60 (dense 0.902, card 0.299) states that it participated in and joins named other submissions, so the agency can treat the filings as one coordinated position. Contrast R20 (dense 0.269, card 0.802), which lists 23 signatory organizations but describes no process at all, and R45 (dense 0.094, card 0.614), which lists coalition members similarly. This is deliberately about described process, not about who the submitter is: the merit signal is that the position has been stress-tested against internal disagreement before it reached the docket.
all_names: Position developed through a described, testable deliberative process

species.name: First-hand fact the record lacks, plus its consequence for the rule
species.instruction: Composite. Score the joint presence of (a) a specific fact from direct experience that could not be read off the docket or the proposal, and (b) an explicit consequence drawn from it for a decision the agency must make. 10 = both present and connected: a particular observed practice, local arrangement, timing, or operational reality is reported, and the comment says what the agency should therefore decide differently. 5 = experience is reported vividly but yields only a general endorsement, objection, or appeal to trust the commenter. 0 = experience is asserted as standing alone ('I have worked in this field for decades') with no fact and no consequence.
species.rationale: R23 (dense 0.789, card 0.143) reports that descendants of an individual land grant hold and use resources as small sole proprietorships, and then draws the consequence: FEMA's definition of 'business loss' will likely fail to recognize them. R54 (dense 0.854, card 0.176) reports the January-February 2020 voluntary stand-down and draws the consequence that a larger combined-season fleet cannot coordinate one, driving Chinook bycatch. R56 (dense 0.826, card 0.292) reports that rear cameras are used in non-backing maneuvers and that monitors have brightness controls, and draws the consequence for the timeout requirement. The failing side is instructive: R06 (dense 0.238, card 0.785) has 30-plus years of permit-holder experience and R43 has 100,000 members' worth of professional standing, but both convert that standing mainly into general endorsement. The scorecard appears to credit the experience; dense appears to credit only experience that pays out in a fact.
all_names: First-hand fact the record lacks, plus its consequence for the rule

species.name: Actionable procedural request with a reason tied to the record
species.instruction: Score whether the comment asks the agency to do something procedural that is within its power, with a stated reason. 10 = a specific procedural action is requested — extend or reopen the comment period, defer action pending analysis, phase the effective date, re-notice, publish a tracking or timeline commitment — with a stated reason grounded in the record or in the requester's circumstances. 5 = process is criticized but no request is made, or a request is made with no reason. 0 = no procedural dimension.
species.rationale: R57 (dense 0.932, card 0.399) is the sharpest case in the slice: it does almost nothing except request a 60-day extension so that comments can be completed, and dense puts it in the top 7 percent while the card puts it in the bottom 40. R24 (dense 0.835, card 0.260) makes the same move with a reason the agency could not have supplied itself — that soliciting comment at the height of the summer fishing season excludes the people on the water daily from June through October. R14 asks for an application status tracking system with published review timelines. A procedural ask is cheap to grant and directly changes the proceeding, which is plausibly why the dense model weights it and a merit-of-argument bank does not.
all_names: Actionable procedural request with a reason tied to the record

species.name: Calibrated partial agreement that isolates exactly the disputed provision
species.instruction: Score how precisely the comment separates what it accepts from what it disputes. 10 = the comment explicitly endorses identified parts of the proposal (including its goal or the reasoning behind it) and then localizes its objection to a named provision, parameter, or subset of cases, so the agency can see the minimal change requested. 5 = a general 'I support this but' with the objection left diffuse. 0 = undifferentiated support or undifferentiated opposition to the whole action.
species.rationale: R04 (dense 0.758, card 0.267) endorses the Class E designation and calls the 6.4-mile radius reasonable, then localizes: add AWOS/ASOS for METARs, and examine the interaction with operations at the neighboring Class C at GRR. R18 (dense 0.685, card 0.184) agrees that extending the model into early pregnancy captures a genuinely vulnerable window, and disputes only the quality of the data used to do it. R01 accepts the integration effort in principle and objects to the count-versus-weight consequences. R27 shows the same discipline from the card-high side. Contrast the undifferentiated R33 and R30. Calibrated concession is what makes a comment usable in a final-rule response, and it is easy for a bank to score as weak advocacy.
all_names: Calibrated partial agreement that isolates exactly the disputed provision

species.name: Load-bearing quantities that are sourced and checkable
species.instruction: Score whether the numbers in the comment carry the argument and can be verified. 10 = quantities appear with units and a traceable source (named study, report, table, page, docket, or the commenter's own recorded operations), and removing them would collapse the argument. 5 = numbers are present and relevant but unsourced, or sourced but decorative. 0 = no quantities, or quantities that are unsourced and merely rhetorical.
species.rationale: R54 (dense 0.854, card 0.176) cites the AFA Review Document at page 174, Table 17, gives GOA non-exempt sideboard limits to four decimals, and contrasts 2.7 C against a 40-year 3.7 C average and 92.33% against 74.72% pre-spawning — every number is doing work. R11 (dense 0.895, card 0.380) reproduces NHTSA's 2 Hz to 10 Hz and 50/90/99 percent capture figures from the agency's own study. R29 sets 127 recorded SPOT deaths against 2,214 conservatively identified by SIGAR with the report linked. The over-credit direction is visible too: R31 (card 0.998) quotes an unnamed 'report' and R46 (card 0.644) asserts one million animals killed per day with no source, and both are scored high by the card. Presence of numbers or of a quotation appears to be rewarded where sourcing and load-bearing-ness are not.
all_names: Load-bearing quantities that are sourced and checkable

species.name: Anticipates and answers the strongest contrary rationale
species.instruction: Score whether the comment engages the best argument on the other side rather than only its own. 10 = the comment states the opposing rationale (the agency's, another commenter's, or the obvious objection) accurately and in its strongest form, then answers it on its own terms. 5 = an opposing point is acknowledged and waved off without an answer. 0 = the comment argues one side only, as if no reasonable contrary view existed.
species.rationale: R54 (dense 0.854, card 0.176) explicitly raises the roe-quality argument made by other commenters, grants that maturity has run early in recent years, and answers it with evidence that the temperature anomaly is reverting. R56 (dense 0.826, card 0.292) states the distraction objection attributed to manufacturers and answers it with the brightness and screen-off controls. R47 takes the proposal's own economic-benefit case and nets the added leakage cost against the claimed savings. R10 (dense 0.769, card 0.224) concedes outright that increasing security reduces liberty before arguing why the tradeoff is acceptable for classified enterprise data. The card-high rows R38, R31, R55 are one-sided throughout, and R38 in particular reads as a talking-points list with no opposing view in view at all.
all_names: Anticipates and answers the strongest contrary rationale

species.name: Every claim bears on a decision this rulemaking must make
species.instruction: Score the fraction of the comment's substantive content that is responsive to the question actually before the agency in this proceeding. 10 = every claim and request maps to a determination the agency has to make in this action; nothing is adjacent policy grievance or expressive material. 5 = a responsive core surrounded by substantial off-question material, or a responsive position argued mostly through unrelated concerns. 0 = the comment is about a different policy question, or is expressive or rhetorical without a request the agency could act on in this docket.
species.rationale: This is the clearest over-credit direction in the slice. R31 sits at card_pct=0.998 — the top of the bank — while arguing in a harvest-specifications docket that offshore wind should be banned, which is not a determination before that agency in that action. R36 (card 0.933) is a poem about losing a home to wildfire, with real emotional force and no request. R30 (card 0.891) is a single garbled line of product endorsement. R42 (dense 0.722, card 0.092) fails the same test from the other side by recasting color standards for carrots as an epochal shift in the agricultural economy. High-end anchors are R32, R50, and R12, where every paragraph lands on something the agency has to resolve. A bank that rewards vividness, quotation, stated stake, or clear position independently of responsiveness will systematically overrate the R31/R36/R30 family.
all_names: Every claim bears on a decision this rulemaking must make

species.name: Rule-text anchoring
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment pinpoints multiple proposed provisions and explains their operation; score 0 when it offers only generic policy sentiment without engaging the proposal.
species.rationale: R18, R40, and R57 engage specific technical provisions, whereas R29 and R53 largely express support or opposition without analyzing rule text.

species.name: Traceable, relevant evidence
species.instruction: Score 10 when claims are supported by identifiable studies, records, measurements, or data directly relevant to the proposal; score 0 when claims rely only on unsupported assertion or rhetoric.
species.rationale: R18 cites experimental studies tied to invasion mechanisms, R22 scrutinizes epidemiological inputs, and R50 references a study’s limited scope; R08 and R33 provide essentially no verifiable support.

species.name: Evidence critique and uncertainty calibration
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes strong evidence from weak evidence, identifies assumptions or limitations, and calibrates confidence; score 0 when it treats all claims as certain or ignores contrary evidence.
species.rationale: R18 identifies missing biological research and limits of extrapolation, R22 questions model-data quality, and R37 distinguishes observed trends from uncertain long-term patterns; R20 presents many consequential claims without comparable qualification.

species.name: Quantified impact and baseline comparison
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment quantifies effects and compares them with a baseline, alternative, or relevant historical level; score 0 when impacts are described only with vague intensifiers.
species.rationale: R04 uses capture percentages to justify a recording duration, R24 quantifies savings and leakage costs, and R37 compares catch, temperature, and maturity data; R30 and R53 mostly use unquantified urgency.

species.name: Operational implementability
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies responsible actors, workflows, training, system dependencies, or failure modes that determine whether the rule can work in practice; score 0 when implementation is treated as automatic.
species.rationale: R07 analyzes HVAC, power-transfer, testing, and alarm workflows, while R44 asks who will train providers and route forms across military services.

species.name: Failure-mode and edge-case analysis
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment examines foreseeable failure conditions, unusual operating contexts, secondary effects, and safeguards; score 0 when it discusses only normal or ideal operation.
species.rationale: R57 analyzes power-transfer, airflow-reversal, and control-system failures, R27 identifies night-driving and delivery-operation issues, and R09 describes nighttime UAS safeguards; R31 offers no comparable operational analysis.

species.name: Cross-rule and system consistency
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies interactions, conflicts, duplicated requirements, or coordination needs across related rules, agencies, or workflows; score 0 when it treats the proposal in isolation.
species.rationale: R47 compares overlapping aircraft directives, R59 addresses conflicting product classifications, and R50 distinguishes risks across tax forms; R39 notes neighboring airspace but develops the interaction only partially.

species.name: Legal authority and interpretive fit
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accurately connects the proposal to statutory language, delegated authority, precedent, or applicable legal limits; score 0 when legal conclusions are asserted without textual or doctrinal support.
species.rationale: R42 invokes and applies Supreme Court interpretation, R28 analyzes statutory authority and rulemaking requirements, and R56 connects discretion to constitutional and APA concerns; R15 raises legal objections but leaves them largely unspecified.

species.name: Distributional incidence and equity
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which populations, firms, places, or users bear distinct costs and benefits and explains unequal exposure or access; score 0 when effects are described only for an undifferentiated public.
species.rationale: R07 explains how reimbursement affects older Medicare patients’ access, R20 connects vaccine access to children and immunocompromised households, and R30 identifies lead burdens in vulnerable communities; R44 discusses consumers and producers only abstractly.

species.name: Dynamic and long-horizon consequences
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment addresses timing, transition, behavioral adaptation, cumulative effects, or consequences unfolding over years; score 0 when it considers only an immediate static effect.
species.rationale: R32 discusses monitoring and habitat management over decades, R37 analyzes seasonal timing and changing ocean conditions, and R55 addresses long-lived infrastructure; R36 mainly asserts future growth without analyzing its dynamics.

species.name: Monitoring, verification, and feedback design
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes measurable indicators, data collection, verification methods, reporting, or triggers for revisiting the approach; score 0 when it offers no way to test or track performance.
species.rationale: R16 calls for complete public casualty data, R32 requires sustained monitoring with funding, R40 warns that unreliable coding corrupts later analysis, and R57 specifies acceptable verification evidence; R53 supplies no measurement framework.

species.name: Generalized firsthand evidence
species.instruction: Score 10 when personal experience supplies concrete observations and is translated into a rule-relevant, potentially generalizable pattern; score 0 when it is only anecdote, praise, or emotion without analyzable detail.
species.rationale: R01 connects lived exposure to pollution with specific accountability and air-quality mechanisms, whereas R05 provides positive travel experience without evidence about the regulatory question.

species.name: Counterargument and tradeoff handling
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment recognizes serious competing objectives or objections, compares them explicitly, and explains why its recommended balance is preferable; score 0 when it relies on one-sided advocacy without addressing tradeoffs.
species.rationale: R19 weighs security against liberty, R21 weighs prescribed-fire benefits against smoke concerns, R24 weighs compliance savings against leakage costs, and R60 weighs risk reduction against financing and market effects.

species.name: Rule-text pinpointing
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies an exact proposed provision and specifies a concrete revision; score 0 when it only expresses support or opposition without an identifiable rule-text target.
species.rationale: R17 pinpoints conflicting compliance deadlines, while R03 requests a broader boundary without analyzing specific proposed language.

species.name: Uncertainty calibration
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment clearly separates established facts, inferences, assumptions, and unresolved uncertainty; score 0 when it presents speculation or contested claims as certain.
species.rationale: R14 distinguishes documented findings from prediction difficulties, while R41 shifts among strong assertions, personal worries, and uncertainty without a stable evidentiary boundary.

species.name: Edge-case coverage
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies materially different contexts or affected populations and explains why the proposed approach may operate differently in each; score 0 when it assumes a homogeneous setting.
species.rationale: R06 distinguishes workers by age and disability, and R38 identifies different radiopharmaceutical settings, products, and patient-access conditions.

species.name: Tradeoff accounting
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment weighs competing benefits, costs, risks, and affected parties with an explicit comparison; score 0 when it presents only one-sided benefits, harms, or political preferences.
species.rationale: R13 compares risk reduction against financing and market effects, while R48 weighs compliance savings against leakage and climate consequences.

species.name: Temporal transition reasoning
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment analyzes timing, sequencing, phase-in, duration, seasonal variation, or changing conditions and connects them to the rule’s effects; score 0 when timing is ignored.
species.rationale: R17 identifies conflicting 24- and 60-month compliance periods, and R18 explains how season timing, temperature, and fish movement affect bycatch and participation.

species.name: Interaction and spillovers
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces consequences across connected systems, actors, jurisdictions, or environmental processes, including meaningful second-order effects; score 0 when it considers only the immediate direct effect.
species.rationale: R18 connects season consolidation to vessel participation, fishing timing, quota use, and Chinook bycatch, while R28 links roads and corridors to migration, collisions, genetics, and climate adaptation.

species.name: Scope prioritization
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment separates the central issue from tangents, ranks its recommendations, and gives a decision-ready conclusion; score 0 when it is diffuse, internally unfocused, or consists mainly of generic requests.
species.rationale: R45 isolates a precise reporting ambiguity and asks a focused interpretive question, while R49 lists broad review goals without prioritizing a concrete regulatory decision.
